title: $W^*$-categories are von Neumann
summary: A $C^*$-category is to a $C^*$-algebra what a groupoid is to a group. An example is the category of Hilbert spaces and bounded linear maps, and indeed, every $C^*$-category can be represented as a sub-$*$-category of this. Analogously, a $W^*$-category is a $C^*$-category where every object has a predual, and we might expect a representation theory on Hilbert spaces where the resulting morphism spaces are $σ$-weakly closed.
